def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # The puzzle is split by solid horizontal and vertical lines of one divider color.
    row_divs = [r for r, row in enumerate(grid) if len(set(row)) == 1]
    col_divs = [c for c in range(w) if len({grid[r][c] for r in range(h)}) == 1]
    # Keep only lines whose color is shared by both divider directions.
    common = {grid[r][0] for r in row_divs} & {grid[0][c] for c in col_divs}
    if common:
        divider = next(iter(common))
        row_divs = [r for r in row_divs if grid[r][0] == divider]
        col_divs = [c for c in col_divs if grid[0][c] == divider]
    rb = [-1] + row_divs + [h]
    cb = [-1] + col_divs + [w]
    rs = [(rb[i] + 1, rb[i + 1]) for i in range(len(rb) - 1)]
    cs = [(cb[i] + 1, cb[i + 1]) for i in range(len(cb) - 1)]

    # The panel containing the motif is the one with the most cells unlike its background.
    panels = []
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(rs):
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(cs):
            vals = [grid[r][c] for r in range(r0, r1) for c in range(c0, c1)]
            bg = max(set(vals), key=vals.count)
            marks = [(r - r0, c - c0, grid[r][c])
                     for r in range(r0, r1) for c in range(c0, c1)
                     if grid[r][c] != bg]
            panels.append((len(marks), ri, ci, bg, marks))
    _, src_ri, src_ci, bg, marks = max(panels, key=lambda p: p[0])

    out = [row[:] for row in grid]
    src_w = cs[src_ci][1] - cs[src_ci][0]
    for ri, (r0, r1) in enumerate(rs):
        for ci, (c0, c1) in enumerate(cs):
            if (ri, ci) == (src_ri, src_ci):
                continue
            dst_w = c1 - c0
            for dr, dc, color in marks:
                # Copy the source motif in the same local orientation into every panel.
                if r0 + dr < r1 and dc < dst_w:
                    out[r0 + dr][c0 + dc] = color
    return out
